analysis:
This batch has only documentation changes: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/ssd-concurrent-checkpoint-restores.md, lines 3-5) and an added paragraph in docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (head lines ~802-810) plus a date bump. No source code is supplied, so I examined the documented behavior against T-041 (SSD prefix-cache at-rest tier, SEC-035) and its mitigations.

Documented behavior changes: concurrent restores of one complete checkpoint share a per-file lease and read in parallel. Writers, duplicate validation and maintenance take the lease exclusively. Readers rewrite the mtime or remove a corrupt file only while holding the file alone, and at most once per ttlSeconds/30. Whole-root TTL maintenance consults the loaded store's in-memory last-hit before deleting a file and records a newer hit as the mtime.

Security-relevant observations, none a concrete regression from this evidence:
- The 30-minute sliding TTL bound in T-041 still holds, but mtime can now trail the last hit. Disk-budget LRU eviction still orders by mtime, so it can evict recently hit files. This is an availability and efficiency matter, not a confidentiality one.
- The changelog states that a provider restart in the minute before maintenance can drop a file whose mtime is stale. This errs toward earlier deletion, which is conservative for at-rest exposure. The in-memory last-hit gate only extends retention within the TTL.
- Authentication, HMAC naming, cacheSalt scoping and the KEK purge are unchanged per the docs. Parallel reads of one authenticated file do not change the per-account cacheSalt isolation.
- The docs say a corrupt-file removal is performed only when the reader holds the file alone. That is a concurrency-safety claim.

Integration questions for the code-bearing passes: confirm the lease implementation (writer-preferring queue, no reader starvation or writer deadlock), that the mtime-rewrite and corrupt-removal paths cannot race a writer or maintenance, and that the in-memory last-hit TTL check in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift cannot keep a file past TTL. The same-account TTFT oracle in SEC-035 is unchanged in kind, though parallel restore timing might marginally alter observable hit latency. Source for these Swift files was not supplied, so those contracts are unverified.
